title: HarnessDomain
description: The CENTRAL domain registry of the pure-skill architecture. Every shared field that crosses a skill boundary is defined here exactly once, with its meaning, owner, and storage tier annotated — work-order.schema.json and work-result.schema.json $ref into $defs below instead of re-defining records inline, and no skill may introduce a cross-boundary field that is not registered here first. Annotation keys: x-tier = SHARED (committed under shapeup/, survives clone+crash) | LOCAL (gitignored under .shapeup/, regenerable run-trace) | EMBEDDED (a record type that only lives inside another entity); x-location = the canonical path; x-writer = the single component allowed to write it; x-readers = who consumes it. The x-erd block is the machine-readable entity-relationship map; x-payload-by-worker is the authoritative table of which WorkOrder payload fields each worker may rely on.

x-erd.description: Relationship map. Cardinality reads left-to-right (WorkOrder 1:1 WorkResult = every order has exactly one result). Join keys: <slug> (the feature) is the aggregate root every path is keyed off; scope_id is the STABLE cross-machine key (boards regenerate; T0 history and branches join on it); TASK-NNN ids are machine-local and must never be joined across machines (board regeneration joins on scope, not task id).

x-payload-by-worker.description: Which WorkOrderPayload fields each worker may rely on, per its SKILL.md input contract. Every name listed here MUST exist in $defs/WorkOrderPayload/properties (structural test enforced). A worker treats any field absent from its order as unknown — never inferred.

x-result-by-worker.description: Which WorkResult fields each worker is allowed to output. A worker must only return fields explicitly mapped here (e.g., spec-evaluator is the sole judge and only it may return a verdict; task-executor is the only one to return task_results).

WorkerName.description: The complete worker roster — the only skills a dispatch may be addressed to. building (the loop) and shapeup are deliberately absent (the orchestrator and PO-personal shaping are not workers); the loop appears in an order only as the `worker` of a fence-only `plan` order, which the order schema accepts beside this roster.

Operation.description: The full operation vocabulary. Replaces lifecycle flags (--tasks-only, --from-discovered, --map-scopes …): the caller knows the pipeline position; the worker never re-derives it. Ownership: execute/fix = task-executor · plan = the loop itself, a fence-only order no sub-agent answers (one per planning substep: requirements, spec, wire, scopes) · evaluate = spec-evaluator · orient = orient · hunt = qa-edge-hunter. The stop census, the retro and the intake's language gate are the loop's own acts and carry no order at all.

Substrate.description: The write contract of one order — mode/flag differences ARE write-contract differences (one whitelist template per operation, the loop substrateFor()). Enforced mechanically by the sandbox hook; a worker needing a file outside it must ESCALATE (substrate-expansion), never write.
Substrate.x-writer: the loop (templates in its orders resource) / the loop's plan activity, scopes substep (per-scope globs)

allowed.description: Globs the worker MAY write. For build attempts: the scope's allowed_file_substrate.

shared.description: Globs ≥2 scopes both touch — an edit here is read-modify-write, so two scopes that both declare one never build at the same time.

append_only.description: Sections that may only grow (e.g. usecases/*.md#Invariants, #Test Surface during reconcile).

frozen.description: Explicitly untouchable paths (spec core: domain-model, UC Steps, contracts, ux-behavior). A build leg's order freezes the whole run trace here and carves out what it authors through `own`: a freeze that lists the channels a defect happened to name grows one defect at a time and is not a boundary.

own.description: Paths this order may write DESPITE a broader freeze — the loop's grant, derived from the order's own identity and never requested by a worker. For a build leg: its own WorkResult (no sibling's — a leg that can write another's can report work nobody did), its task files, the discovery ledger. Checked BEFORE `frozen`, and only against the contract that declared it, so another live order's exception never licenses this write.

Interaction.description: Caller policy. Pausing is the CALLER's decision — a pure worker only surfaces questions/assumptions; it never decides whether the pipeline stops.

pause_gates.description: true (standalone default): pause at the worker's phase checkpoints. false: run straight through, surfacing questions as assumptions[] — or, when one genuinely blocks, deviations[] with status 'escalated'.

TaskRef.description: One task as carried inside a WorkOrder — parsed from the LOCAL board file (.shapeup/<slug>/tasks/TASK-*.md frontmatter + AC checkboxes) by the loop parseTaskFile(). NOTE: task ids are machine-local (boards regenerate and renumber); never join on id across machines — the scope is the stable key.
TaskRef.x-writer: the loop (from the board the plan activity generated)

body_path.description: Path to the full task file — the worker must read it fully, never rely on this summary alone.

acceptance_criteria.description: The AC checkbox texts, verbatim — the loop ticks boxes by matching this text back. ADDITIVE union (spine v1.3): a plain `string` (legacy boards, unchanged) OR `{text, covers?}` when the board line carries a `(covers: REQ-…)` clause. `.text` stays BYTE-IDENTICAL to the checkbox so the loop's substring tick-back (AcResult.ac) is untouched; `covers[]` is the LOCAL→SHARED anchor the planning read-back reads for covers-closure. A pre-covers board keeps parsing as string[] (the ✦ non-regression invariant).

text.description: The checkbox text, verbatim (byte-identical to the board line — includes any trailing (covers: …) clause).

covers.description: REQ-ids this AC covers — resolved against the SHARED requirements registry by the planning read-back.

status.description: ready | in-progress | blocked | done | cut (board frontmatter; informational inside an order).

depends_on.description: Explicit dependencies. The inverse (unlocks) is ALWAYS derived by the loop, never hand-authored — hand-authored inverses drift asymmetric, observed repeatedly.

use_case_refs.description: UC ids this task implements (e.g. UC-CreateOrder) — the task's LOCAL→SHARED anchor into the committed spec and spec-evaluator's traceability source. Links flow one direction: the LOCAL task cites the SHARED UC; a committed doc never links a task id back (ids are machine-local).

scope_id.description: OPTIONAL: the scope that builds this task. The DISAMBIGUATOR, not the primary link — dispatch normally derives a scope's tasks by intersecting the contract's use_cases[] with this task's use_case_refs[], and that is a partition only while each scope owns its own use cases. When several scopes implement one use case (a four-scope, one-UC cut is ordinary) the UC anchor cannot say who builds what and every scope claims every task; the planning read-back reds that, and this field resolves it. Same sanctioned LOCAL→SHARED direction as use_case_refs: the volatile board names the stable scope_id, never the reverse.

Decision.description: One adjudicated ESCALATE answer as carried inside a WorkOrder — binding precedent the worker must apply. Compiled from the committed round-ledger.md Decisions table (columns: Round | Scope | Kind | Question | Answer | Resolved by) filtered to this scope. The full row lives in the ledger; the envelope carries the minimal {id, answer} projection.
Decision.x-tier: EMBEDDED (projection of the SHARED round-ledger.md Decisions row)
Decision.x-writer: the operator — a PO answer to a blocked worker is filed here by hand, the instant it is given; no kernel step or loop step writes this file (the loop reads it)

AegisTriple.description: One digested failure — the failure digester distills raw build/test/Playwright logs into these so the next attempt gets a few lines of signal instead of a stack-trace dump. Appears as T0Artifact.discovered_tasks[] (red attempts) and as WorkOrder payload.digested_errors[] (the next attempt's starting bug list).
AegisTriple.x-writer: the failure digester, called by harness verify t0 (regex pass only)

file.description: Source file of the failure; null/absent when the log line named no file at all (raw triple — never invented).

line.description: Line of the failure; null/absent when the diagnostic carried no line number — independently of `file`, since a diagnostic can name a file with no line (a resource-compiler error, for example). Never invented to satisfy a shape.

kind.description: Log-format tag (stack | tap | tsc | error | raw).

VerifySpec.description: How the doer proves its work: the verification command the caller pins (task-executor never chooses its own test command in orchestrated mode).

env.description: Env var names the command needs.

Constraints.description: Non-Go items and freezes for a build order. The moment an implementation starts touching a non_go item the worker stops that path and reports — scope expansion is the caller's decision.

non_go.description: Excluded paths/features from the pitch boundaries.

ui_layers.description: e.g. {layer3_frozen: true} — no pixel/CSS polish beyond semantic HTML defaults.

AffordanceEntry.description: One interactive element of a scope's UI, derived from ux-behavior.md state tables. Layer-1 contract: every element the doer builds binds to a manifest test_id/role and expresses its state via data-state; the judge asserts UI affordance-only against this (never pixels — Layer 3 is frozen). An element the manifest lacks is a spec gap → ESCALATE, never a silent extension.

test_id.description: The data-testid the element binds to.

required_states.description: Subset of [idle, loading, success, error, empty] the element must express via data-state.

source.description: The breadboard UI affordance (U#) this element implements; absent without a breadboard.

UseCase.description: One use case — the STABLE anchor both tiers name, and the only identifier the scope↔task relation is re-derived through. A UC id is assigned once and frozen: it behaves like scope_id and REQ-id, never like TASK-NNN. Referenced three ways across the tree (`UC-x`, `[[UC-x]]`, `[[usecases/UC-x]]`); `kernel/core/contract.mjs` ucId() is the single normaliser, and both sides of any join must pass through it or they disagree about a UC they both hold.
UseCase.x-writer: the loop's plan activity, spec substep (a reconcile pass MAY append, never renumber)
UseCase.x-readers: the plan activity (scopes: use_cases[]; wire: wiring-map entries), spec-evaluator (the grading criterion), the loop's planning read-back (SCOPE-ANCHOR + UC-ANCHOR)

id.description: `UC-*`, matching the filename stem. Frozen once assigned — every use_cases[] and use_case_refs[] link rots if it is renumbered.

invariants.description: `[INV-NN]` markers declared in the body; the source of regression tasks and Test Surface rows.

ScopeContract.description: A vertical scope as a committed, mechanically enforceable contract — Shape Up's 'map the scopes' as data. Sliced by business flow (one call chain: UI screen + API route + use case + repository), NEVER by directory (PA1). The sandbox hook enforces the substrate, t0-verify runs the fixtures, the evaluator asserts against the manifest. Superseded contracts are kept, never deleted (branch and T0 history stay attributable). ON-DISK FORMAT IS MARKDOWN: frontmatter carries the scalars and [a, b] lists, a markdown table carries the one array-of-objects field, and prose carries the rationale a reviewer reads. THIS SCHEMA DESCRIBES THE PARSED OBJECT — the wire form embedded in the WorkOrder envelope — not the file. `kernel/core/contract.mjs` is the only reader/writer of the file form; everything downstream of that parse sees exactly this shape.
ScopeContract.x-writer: the loop's plan activity, scopes substep (SOLE writer — a hand-edit anywhere else is a defect)
ScopeContract.x-readers: the loop, sandbox-guard hook, harness verify t0, the loop's planning read-back, spec-evaluator, the stop census, the loop

scope_id.description: The STABLE cross-machine join key: hill shards, T0 verdicts, branches, and decisions all key on it (task ids renumber per machine; this never does).

topology_type.description: LAYER_CAKE = thin balanced UI+backend · ICEBERG = complexity on one side · CHOWDER = true strays with no shared flow (the one deliberate exception to cross-layer slicing).

use_cases.description: The COMMITTED use cases this scope implements (`UC-*`, resolving to spec/usecases/UC-*.md) — the scope's anchor into the spec and the join the scope↔task relation is re-derived through. Mirrors the board's own `use_case_refs` in the sanctioned LOCAL→SHARED direction. This REPLACES the former `tasks[]` id list: a contract is committed and a board is not, so naming task ids put a pointer into a gitignored, per-machine tier that resolved to nothing on every other clone without a single check going red. the planning read-back reds an empty or unresolvable anchor.

covers.description: Optional REQ-ids from requirements.md this scope answers for — the same stable, never-renumbered key an AC's `covers:` clause uses. Projected as the Scope→Requirement COVERS edge in the run graph.

depends_on.description: scope_ids this scope must build AFTER. Build order lives in the same tier as the contracts it orders: this was previously derived from the LOCAL board (contract tasks → task depends_on → owning scope), which collapsed to no edges whenever the board was absent and silently degraded the scheduler to an unscheduled fan-out. An id naming a scope not in the run is dropped by the scheduler (fail-open) and reported by spec-lint SCOPE-DEPS.

allowed_file_substrate.description: Exact write-whitelist globs — the sandbox hook's deny list boundary. Wrong here = a legitimate ESCALATE later.

shared_substrate.description: Files ≥2 scopes both touch — must be declared in BOTH scopes' lists (the DISJOINT rule); declaring one costs concurrency, since two scopes that share a path build one at a time.

affordance_manifest.description: Every interactive element of this scope's screens — appears in exactly ONE scope's manifest.

e2e_verification_fixtures.description: Command(s) that drive this scope end-to-end (the T0 layer). EACH MUST EXIT 0 WHEN THE SCOPE IS CORRECT — `harness verify t0` scores a fixture as failed on any non-zero exit, so a fixture written as a bare error-path invocation (`todo done abc  # exit 1`) can never pass and the scope can never go T0-green however correct the code is. Assert error paths INSIDE a test file that itself exits 0 (`node --test test/commands/done.test.js`), which is what the expected non-zero exit belongs in. Too speculative to fixture → an explicit TBD flag, never an invented fixture.

db_probe.description: Optional command asserting real persisted state (catches the hardcoded-array Layer-2 violation). Absent = not applicable, never a failure.

hill_phase.description: ALWAYS authored as UPHILL_UNKNOWN — self-reported confidence is the risk this closes. The live phase is DERIVED from T0/T1 facts into hill/<scope-id>.yml — facts move dots, not authors.

superseded_by.description: Set by map-scopes: the replacing scope ids. Supersede-never-delete.

business_goal.description: What a user can do when this scope ships — the must-have trace the stop census checks against.

ScopeBoard.description: The scope board — a HUMAN-READABLE PROJECTION of the contracts, not a source. Every column restates something `scopes/*.md` already declares, so it can be regenerated from them and deleting it loses nothing. It deliberately carries no `wave` column: waves are Kahn levels of `depends_on` and the loop derives them, and a hand-authored copy of a derived value is the same defect as the hand-authored `unlocks` that `deriveUnlocks` exists to prevent. Nothing parses this file — that is only safe while it stays a view; the moment it holds a fact of its own it needs a reader and a lint like every other contract.
ScopeBoard.x-writer: the loop's plan activity, scopes substep (regenerated whenever the contracts change)
ScopeBoard.x-readers: humans, in a pull request. No code reads it — by design.

rows.description: One row per scope: scope_id · topology_type · use_cases · depends_on · substrate size · lint status. All projected from the contract.

AcResult.description: One acceptance criterion's outcome with evidence. 'ac' carries the checkbox text VERBATIM — the loop ticks boxes by substring-matching it. No recorded evidence = the worker reports fail by its own hand.

ac.description: The AC checkbox text, verbatim from the task file.

evidence.description: Concrete observable proof (command output, response, snapshot path).

TaskResult.description: Per-task outcome inside a WorkResult. the loop flips the board row, ticks pass ACs, sets frontmatter status/completed_at, and appends the Execution Log from these entries — the worker itself writes none of that.

FileTouched.description: One file the worker created/modified/deleted — audit data for the run ledger; also how the orchestrator sees substrate usage.

Discovery.description: The universal currency of surprise: one raw discovered line. Producers: task-executor (marker +, P3.7), qa-edge-hunter (always ~, repro required), the plan activity (overflow reports). NO producer writes the ledger — the loop appends every entry to discovery/ledger.md (single-writer, mechanically). Promotion ~ → must-have is always a human act at SHIP S.0/GATE H.
Discovery.x-tier: EMBEDDED (projection into the LOCAL discovery ledger)
Discovery.x-readers: the plan activity (spec reconcile mode, scopes), the stop census, qa-edge-hunter (covered-territory context)

marker.description: + = candidate work (build discoveries) · ~ = nice-to-have (all QA findings are born ~).

line.description: One raw line, e.g. "[QA-003] [UC-04] Double-click Confirm creates 2 orders".

lens.description: QA lens tag (①boundary ②concurrency ③interruption ④cross-UC ⑤no-go ⑥residue).

repro.description: Numbered repro steps — mandatory for QA findings (no repro = unconfirmed observation, not a finding).

severity_hint.description: data-integrity | boundary-breach | ux-degradation | cosmetic — the Hunter's ADVICE to triage, never a decision.

test_gap.description: unit | integration | exploratory-only — advises reconciliation whether to generate a test-writing task.

contradicts.description: EVAL criterion id this finding disproves — routes back through triage; the judge's record itself is never edited.

traces_to.description: OPTIONAL (spine v1.3) — REQ-ids this finding maps back to. The checkable back-link (LOCAL→SHARED) so an edge case maps to a business requirement by id instead of grepping ledger.md; `verify spec` only checks the id resolves in the registry.

T0Citation.description: The judge's pointer to a mechanical T0 artifact. The evaluator RECOMPUTES sha256 from disk — a handed hash is never trusted; a verdict on a scoped spec without a citation is structurally invalid: T0 is a machine fact the generator cannot fabricate.

CriterionVerdict.description: One graded criterion. Ingest appends these as VerdictLedgerLine rows to evaluation/.verdicts-<target>.jsonl (append-only — history is how a single-snapshot judge becomes measurable; a flip vs a prior run forces confidence low). A FAIL additionally REQUIRES an evidence locator (file:line) — findings must be actionable without re-investigation.

criterion.description: Traces to committed spec text (UC step/error/invariant/TS row, domain rule, contract field, Done-when, Non-Go) — never a task file's paraphrase.

dimension.description: spec-conformance (default) | tdd-surface | integration | completeness | test-surface-conformance | security | performance.

reprobed.description: Every FAIL is re-probed once before finalizing.

evidence.description: Probe output / file:line — 'NO EVIDENCE' fails the criterion.

traces_to.description: OPTIONAL (spine v1.3) — REQ-ids this criterion maps back to. A checkable finding→requirement anchor (LOCAL→SHARED) so the judge's record maps to a business requirement by id; the planning read-back only checks each id resolves in the registry. Navigation aid, never a grading input.

criterion.description: Traces to committed spec text (UC step/error/invariant/TS row, domain rule, contract field, Done-when, Non-Go) — never a task file's paraphrase.

dimension.description: spec-conformance (default) | tdd-surface | integration | completeness | test-surface-conformance | security | performance.

reprobed.description: Every FAIL is re-probed once before finalizing.

evidence.description: A FAIL must carry a file:line locator. The rule used to live in prose and be enforced nowhere — a correct FAIL verdict with no locator anywhere is unactionable without re-investigating (observed, not theorized). Now mechanical: the loop's result check rejects it before it applies the result.

traces_to.description: OPTIONAL (spine v1.3) — REQ-ids this criterion maps back to. A checkable finding→requirement anchor (LOCAL→SHARED) so the judge's record maps to a business requirement by id; the planning read-back only checks each id resolves in the registry. Navigation aid, never a grading input.

RefutedAc.description: An AC box the judge's evidence disproves. Un-ticking is the loop's act (the judge never touches a task file): the loop un-ticks the box and stamps eval_verdict: fail + eval_at on the task frontmatter.

ac.description: The checkbox text the evidence disproves, verbatim.

Verdict.description: The single judge's return — spec-evaluator only. Overall PASS requires ALL active dimensions to pass (halo effect banned); the judge NEVER sets a task done — closure belongs to the orchestrator.

bugs.description: report-schema bug entries: severity, criterion, file:line, repro, expected vs actual.

CommandResult.description: One executed command's outcome inside a T0 artifact — produced by actually running the command; no agent can fabricate it. It carries the EVIDENCE, not only the score: `exit` maps a command that never started onto the same 1 a real failure returns, so without `error` a refused or timed-out command and a broken build are the same record everywhere downstream, and without the output a verdict asserting `exit 1` is an assertion nobody can check.

exit.description: The process exit code, or 1 when the command never produced one. Not a discriminator on its own — read `error` to tell a crash from a failure.

error.description: Present ONLY when the command did not run to completion — a spawn failure, a maxBuffer overflow, or the 10-minute timeout. Its presence is the fact the ratchet grades as `crash` (tree restored, never counted as a reverted attempt); its absence means the command ran and the exit code is its own.

stdout_tail.description: The last 4000 characters of stdout, omitted when nothing was printed. Kept for passing commands too: a fixture that exits 0 having run zero tests is the false green this layer exists to catch. A truncated tail carries a leading `[truncated: kept the last N of M characters]` line, so a partial stream never reads as a complete one.

stderr_tail.description: The last 4000 characters of stderr, same bound and same truncation marker as `stdout_tail`.

T0Artifact.description: The mechanical verification verdict for one build attempt — the evidence layer under the LLM judge. Written by harness verify t0 from actually running the scope's fixtures and DB probe; zero LLM tokens. spec-evaluator must cite it (sha256) on scoped specs. Red artifacts carry AEGIS triples that become the next attempt's digested_errors.
T0Artifact.x-location: .shapeup/<slug>/t0/verdicts/r<N>-a<M>-t<T>.json (schema_version 2; the unsuffixed r<N>-a<M>.json of schema_version 1 is still readable)
T0Artifact.x-readers: the loop (next attempt), spec-evaluator (citation), the stop census (stall census)

trial.description: schema_version 2+: the retry ordinal within (round, attempt). Written with flag 'wx', so a retry of the SAME attempt lands beside its predecessor instead of destroying it (invariant I4).

run_id.description: OPTIONAL (v1.8) — the run key (mintRunId in lib/paths.mjs). (round, attempt, trial) addresses an artifact within a run and repeats in the next one, so the evidence layer needed this to be groupable by run.

db_probe_green.description: true when no probe declared (null probe never counts as failure).

score.description: schema_version 2+: the comparable outcome vector better() ranks. A reduce over fixtures[] — no new measurement.

discovered_tasks.description: Populated only on red; feeds the next order.

env.description: Where the fixtures ran — host, cwd, git tree, resolved toolchain paths, lockfile digests, profile-declared cache dirs, and a digest over an allowlist of environment variable VALUES (names in the clear, values never stored). `env_sha256` digests the whole block, so a reader compares one field and a human diffs the rest: two verdicts with the same tree and different digests were measured on different machines, which is a fact about portability rather than a regression. Written by kernel/core/env.mjs, which judges nothing — no field here makes a verdict green or red.

host.description: platform, arch, os_release, node, hostname_sha256 (hashed — equality is all a reader needs).

cwd.description: Absolute: a path-keyed toolchain cache is identified by this.

tree.description: git head, branch, and a dirty flag — which says something differs, never what.

toolchain.description: Each invoked binary as written, and where it resolved on this machine (null when nothing resolved it).

lockfiles.description: Digest per lockfile present at the root. Says what was declared, never what is installed.

caches.description: Cache dirs the project profile declares, resolved. null means the profile declared none — NOT that there are none.

env.description: The allowlist of variable names, and one digest over their values.

T0Score.description: The comparable T0 outcome — a VECTOR, not a float, because the three arms are not fungible. Ranked by t0-verify's better(): regressions dominate, then fixtures_passed, then db_probe; a tie is NOT better (a tie counted as an improvement makes a sawtooth look like a ratchet), and a different fixtures_total is INCOMPARABLE rather than worse (a scope split changes the denominator).

fixtures_total.description: The denominator. A change here makes two scores incomparable — better() returns null and the ratchet re-baselines.

db_probe.description: null = no probe declared, which is an absence and never a failure.

TrialRow.description: One row per T0 run — the ratchet's history, and the artifact that makes 'is attempt N+1 better than attempt N?' answerable. Append-only (I4: every superseded object remains addressable). baseline_trial is the parent link: that single field IS the experiment DAG (lineage, PARENT_OF, and a genuine SUPERSEDES edge) delivered without a graph store. Written by t0-verify, NOT the loop: a trial row is a mechanical fact produced by running commands, in the same class as the verdict artifact t0-verify already owns, and carries no worker claim to apply.
TrialRow.x-readers: the loop (payload.trial_history — the paper's inspect()), the loop (the ratchet block of the ship report: improvement_rate, monotone_rate, sawtooth_count)

trial.description: Monotone ordinal across the run's whole ledger — what baseline_trial points at.

run_id.description: OPTIONAL (v1.8) — the run key (mintRunId in lib/paths.mjs), read off the receipt in the run root t0-verify was pointed at. `trial` is monotone WITHIN a run and restarts at 1 in the next one, so ratchet history could not be split by run without it.

artifact.description: Path to the T0Artifact this row records, relative to the run root.

sha256.description: The artifact's content hash — the same bytes spec-evaluator re-hashes.

status.description: The one rule that replaced the protocol's two red branches. kept = strictly better (INCLUDING red-but-improved: 2/5 → 4/5 fixtures is kept, and that is the whole ratchet) · reverted = not better, tree restored · rebased = incomparable, baseline reset · crash = a command failed to spawn or timed out, tree restored.

baseline_trial.description: The trial this one was compared against — the parent edge. null on the first trial of a scope.

tree_ref.description: refs/shapeup/<scope_id>/kept — a SHADOW ref, so the harness keeps its convention of never writing commits to the branch under test.

digest.description: This trial's failures, carried forward as the next order's digested_errors.

VerdictLedgerLine.description: One appended line of judge history (JSONL). Never rewritten — flips across runs are detected here and force confidence low. run auto-increments per append batch.

MetricsRow.description: One SHIP-time harvest row (facts only — copied from structured output that already exists; never a newly computed verdict/score, which would be a second judge behind spec-evaluator). Sharded per machine so concurrent runs never merge-conflict.
MetricsRow.x-writer: none — the ship-time harvest step retired with the run script's sequencing; rows an earlier release wrote under .shapeup/metrics/ keep this shape

at.description: OPTIONAL (v1.2) — ISO harvest timestamp; enables a trend over time. Older rows lack it and fall back to shard append order.

run_id.description: OPTIONAL (v1.8) — the run key (mintRunId in lib/paths.mjs), COPIED from the receipt at SHIP S.6. This is the harvest row's only link to the run trace that produced it: everything else here is a count, and `feature_slug` groups runs together rather than apart.

final_audit_score.description: COPIED from the final EVAL report, never re-graded.

attempt_exhaustions.description: OPTIONAL (v1.2) — scopes whose inner attempt_budget tripped this run, COPIED at SHIP S.6 from the queued GATE H hammer proposals (a fact registered at the source; no reader may re-derive it).

slice_count.description: From breadboard B5 — the normalizer/denominator (round_count=4 on a 2-slice feature is alarming; on a 9-slice one it isn't).

ratchet.description: OPTIONAL (v1.5) — the DAY-1 exit measurement, COPIED from the ratchet report over this run's t0/trials.jsonl before the LOCAL trace is wiped. This is the only place the ratchet numbers survive the run, and the only reason they can be compared across machines: `.shapeup/` is gitignored, so a measurement left there answers the question exactly once and then deletes itself. Facts only — every field is a count or a ratio over recorded trial rows, never a grade.

scopes_multi_trial.description: Scopes with ≥2 trials — the denominator that makes the other numbers meaningful. Zero means this run never asked the Day-1 question.

improvement_rate.description: kept ÷ trials after the first. The first trial is the baseline by construction and is excluded.

monotone_rate.description: Scopes whose score never decreased ÷ scopes with ≥2 trials. A monotone series is a ratchet working; a sawtooth says the loop is still a budgeted retry loop.

hooks.description: OPTIONAL (v1.5) — the DAY-2 exit measurement, COPIED from the hook decision ledger, .shapeup/decisions.jsonl. Makes 'never had to fire' and 'never ran' separable across runs: before the decision ledger both produced exit 0 and empty stdout, which is why several enforcement tools were unscoreable.

sources.description: Paths of the SHARED source artifacts harvested from — SHARED tier ONLY. LOCAL .shapeup/ paths are read at harvest time but never recorded: this row is committed and the run-trace is gitignored/wiped, so a LOCAL path would dangle on every clone (tier-direction rule).

ActiveScopePointer.description: What the sandbox hook reads to enforce the active scope's substrate on every Edit/Write this round. Written at branch checkout; NOT writable by any worker (a worker must never widen its own sandbox).
ActiveScopePointer.x-writer: harness init run (and init run --force when it reopens a closed run); never a worker

SafetyOverrides.description: Escape hatch for the safety-spine hook — a command or secret path matching an entry is exempted from denial (the exemption itself is logged as a SAFETY-OVERRIDE pathology row: overrides stay visible, propose-never-dispose). Malformed file = treated as ABSENT: the override channel fails closed so a parse error can never disable the spine.
SafetyOverrides.x-writer: human PO only — hand-authored. Deliberately placed at the .shapeup/ root, OUTSIDE the active slug's run-trace carve-out, so sandbox-guard denies any worker write to it during a scoped round; safety-spine additionally self-protects the file in every mode.

allow_commands.description: Regex sources; a Bash command matching any is exempted from the spine's deny rules.

allow_secret_paths.description: Globs; a path matching any is exempted from the secret-read deny (Bash readers and the Read tool alike).

note.description: Why the override exists — the audit trail a bare env var could never carry.

RequirementClause.description: One atomic customer requirement, frozen with a STABLE id — the covers-closure input truth (spine v1.3). Extracted from the REQ source (pitch / customer-requirements doc / use-case bodies) by the planner — extraction is judgment (LLM), but ids are assigned ONCE and never renumber (they behave like scope_id, not TASK-NNN — every covers: link would rot otherwise). Supersede-never-delete: a dropped clause is marked CUT (PO-approved), never removed, so the registry stays auditable on a fresh clone. The original REQ source is never edited — the registry is a separate derived, committed file.
RequirementClause.x-writer: the loop's plan activity, requirements substep — extraction only; CUT status is a PO governance edit (same class as a round-ledger Decision)
RequirementClause.x-readers: the loop's planning read-back (covers-closure), the loop (the L1b REQ → AC table), human (coverage/cut audit)

id.description: REQ-N — assigned once, frozen; the stable cross-machine key every covers[] / traces_to[] link resolves against.

clause.description: The requirement text, VERBATIM from the source — the deletion this closure catches is a clause that no AC covers.

source.description: Where the clause came from (e.g. "pitch §2.2", "req-doc.md#L14", "UC-04 body") — the provenance an auditor traces back.

status.description: covered = must be named by ≥1 AC's covers[] or the planning read-back finds it; CUT (PO-approved) = a Betting-Table decision to drop it, kept for audit (never deleted).

note.description: Optional rationale — required in spirit for a CUT (why the clause was dropped).

WiringEntry.description: One use-case's reachability chain inside a WiringMap: engine → wiring seam → entry-point call site → player-visible affordance. The declaration front-loads the integration seam the scopes substep needs at slicing time (the missing input behind the round-1 main.js substrate-expansion escalations).

use_case.description: UC id this chain realizes (e.g. UC-04) — resolves against the committed usecases/ tree.

engine.description: Repo-relative path of the module implementing the UC's core logic — the file the use case's affordance must reach from the entry point.

wiring_seam.description: How the engine is meant to attach (event handler, route registration, init hook) — prose the slicer reads.

entry_call_site.description: DESIGN INTENT (spine v1.3): the composition-root attachment this engine registers into, named from ProjectProfile.entry_point + the mechanism — e.g. 'src/server.ts — POST /checkout route', 'main.js — game-loop init hook'. Symbolic, authored at L1a.5 before the code exists; NEVER an invented file:line. The concrete coordinate is a build-time fact; the evaluator checks it against the running app and nothing parses this field.

affordance.description: The player-visible affordance this UC exposes when wired — the human-facing end of the chain.

Seam.description: How one use case's engine attaches to the entry point — the `wiring_seam` value of a WiringEntry, Not a file: it exists only as a cell in the committed wiring map.
Seam.x-writer: the loop's plan activity, wire substep, inside wiring-map.md

seam.description: The attachment mechanism — a route registration, an event handler, a direct call from the composition root.

engine.description: The repo-relative module the seam attaches.

entry_point.description: The call site the seam reaches from.

WiringMap.description: The reachability map — per UC, the chain from engine to a player-visible affordance (spine v1.3). Written DIRECTLY by the plan activity's wire substep before gate L1a.5 (precedent: ScopeContract is written directly by the scopes substep, bypassing the loop). Its purpose: no engine ships orphaned from the running application — the evaluator and the loop's build and launch check that against the built app. ON-DISK FORMAT IS MARKDOWN: frontmatter carries the scalars and [a, b] lists, a markdown table carries the one array-of-objects field, and prose carries the rationale a reviewer reads. THIS SCHEMA DESCRIBES THE PARSED OBJECT — the wire form embedded in the WorkOrder envelope — not the file. `kernel/core/contract.mjs` is the only reader/writer of the file form; everything downstream of that parse sees exactly this shape.
WiringMap.x-writer: the loop's plan activity, wire substep (SOLE writer, direct — like the scopes substep writes scopes/*.md)
WiringMap.x-readers: the plan activity (scopes: integration seam at slicing time), spec-evaluator

entry_point.description: OPTIONAL echo of ProjectProfile.entry_point at authoring time (informational — the profile stays the source of truth).

ProjectProfile.description: The archetype + entry-point declaration the wiring map and the build probes depend on (spine v1.3). The entry point is archetype-specific (main.js for a client-only game is not the seam for a web-service). SHARED — a declaration that must survive `rm -rf .shapeup/` + clone cannot live in the gitignored run-trace. Role-gating (skip SysRS/Auth/CI-CD) is explicitly OUT of scope — those roles are not workers; the profile is introduced only as the entry-point/archetype declaration. ON-DISK FORMAT IS MARKDOWN: frontmatter carries the scalars and [a, b] lists, a markdown table carries the one array-of-objects field, and prose carries the rationale a reviewer reads. THIS SCHEMA DESCRIBES THE PARSED OBJECT — the wire form embedded in the WorkOrder envelope — not the file. `kernel/core/contract.mjs` is the only reader/writer of the file form; everything downstream of that parse sees exactly this shape.
ProjectProfile.x-writer: the loop, at the intake gate (not the loop, which stays pipeline-blind)
ProjectProfile.x-readers: the loop (build_probe + launch_probe, once per round before EVAL), the plan activity (wire)

archetype.description: Validated against the enum — a typo must FAIL, never silently disable a check.

entry_point.description: The repo-relative seam the wiring map resolves engines against (e.g. main.js, src/server.ts). Not hardcoded — archetype-specific.

note.description: Optional context on the archetype/entry-point choice.

build_probe.description: OPTIONAL — a command that asserts the BUILT ARTIFACT, not the build's exit code, and exits 0 only when it holds. Exists because a green build is not proof the feature compiled: some toolchains compile only the files reachable from an entry point, so a scope's new files can sit outside the compiled set while the build stays green (measured: an app package holding 3 compiled files, 58 errors once the rest became reachable). Archetype-specific by construction — e.g. 'the compiled source map lists every file under each scope's substrate'. Run by the loop (build and launch) after run_cmd, once per round before EVAL; absent = no such step, never a failure.

launch_probe.description: OPTIONAL for most archetypes, EXPECTED for `mobile` — a command that installs the built artifact, starts it, asserts the first screen (ids, text, a screenshot diff) and fails on fatal runtime log patterns. Exists because nothing else in the loop launches the app: a blank first screen survived three EVAL rounds on a run whose every T0 fixture was green. Run by the loop (build and launch) after run_cmd and build_probe; a mobile profile without one should be called out at GATE L0, so the 'on-device install unverified' risk has a named owner. Absent = no such step.

WorkOrderPayload.description: The union of every worker-specific input field a WorkOrder payload may carry. Which fields a given worker relies on is registered in x-payload-by-worker at the schema root — a worker treats anything absent from its order as unknown, and a NEW cross-boundary field must be added HERE first (with an x-payload-by-worker entry), never invented ad hoc in a skill.

scope_contract.description: task-executor: the active scope, verbatim from scopes/<id>.md.

tasks.description: task-executor: what to implement · spec-evaluator: traceability ONLY (never a grading source).

decisions.description: task-executor: binding precedent from prior escalations.

digested_errors.description: task-executor: the previous attempt's failures — the starting bug list.

trial_history.description: task-executor: the paper's inspect() — this scope's recent trials, CROSSING the round boundary (this round and the one before it), each with its score, kept/reverted status and top-3 digest. Absent when no trials.jsonl exists, which is the non-regression path. Token-bounded at 8 rows (~600 tokens) against an attempt_budget of 5 — cheaper than one re-proposed failed change.

kb_rules_path.description: Coachable workers (task-executor, qa-edge-hunter, orient): shapeup/knowledge-base/<skill>.md — steering, never spec and never a gate; conflict → the AC, the contract or the gate wins, noted in deviations. The judge and the census are not coachable.

bugs.description: The previous round's FAIL verdict, addressed to the scope whose substrate contains each cited file — touch nothing else. Written by `the loop` from results/evaluate-r<N-1>.json, never by a caller: a build order is addressed by scope/round/attempt and carries no caller payload, and the verdict must survive the relaunch that separates two rounds. Present on any r≥2 execute order whose predecessor failed; an entry matching no scope's substrate is marked `unowned` and sent to all of them rather than dropped.

spec_folder.description: Planner/judge/QA/architect/orient: the committed spec tree (shapeup/<slug>/spec/). The judge's grading truth.

feature.description: The feature slug — the aggregate-root key of every path.

pitch.description: orient: the kicked-off pitch path (shaped + bet; frontmatter appetite/status/bet).

breadboard.description: orient: the run's staged breadboard — Places (P#), UI and code affordances (U#, N#), stores (S#), slices (V#). Absent = the pitch has no separate breadboard (it may carry one inline); never inferred from the pitch's folder.

stack.description: orient: stack hint aiming the code-surface sweeps (e.g. "pnpm, Next 16 web :3000").

step.description: building (operation: plan): which planning substep this fence order covers. The order's id is plan-<step> and its substrate is that substep's write contract, so each substep leaves its own leg row and its own fence.

mode.description: building (operation: plan, step: spec): how the spec substep is scoped — full (tree + board), board-only (a committed tree is frozen; only the per-machine board is regenerated), reconcile (discovered items fold in; invariants and the Test Surface are append-only), retrofit-surface (append the Test Surface to a spec that predates it). Absent = full.

kb_rules_paths.description: building (operation: plan): the knowledge-base files the planning activity reads — its own (`plan`) and the three it was filed under before the fold (ba-pitch-analyzer, scope-architect, solution-architect). Whether each exists is for the loop to see; steering, never spec and never a gate.

dimensions.description: spec-evaluator: the active dimension set. the loop fills it on every evaluate order: the run's named set, or the set resolved from the spec with the judge's auto-enable rules. Absent only on a standalone order.

run_cmd.description: spec-evaluator: how to start the running app. Absent orchestrated → ESCALATE, never guess.

launch_cmd.description: spec-evaluator, qa-edge-hunter: the project profile's launch probe — installs the built artifact, starts it and asserts the first screen. Derived by `the loop` from project-profile.md, absent when the profile declares none. Where `run_cmd` is only a build, this is how the app is brought up; a non-zero exit is a finding, not a reason to guess another way.

revised_checks.description: spec-evaluator: rows that FAILed in one of the round's T0 trials and PASS in a later one whose own check file (named by the row id) changed in between. Derived by the loop. Each must be read against its row before its PASS counts; absent when none.

scopes_without_t0.description: spec-evaluator: scopes whose contract exists but which hold no green T0 verdict for the round, while at least one other scope does. Derived by the loop. The round is still gradeable: each row such a scope owns is a FAIL citing the scope contract, never a reason to refuse the round. Absent when every scope is green.

build_gate.description: spec-evaluator, qa-edge-hunter: this run's newest round build gate artifact (build/r<N>-t<T>.json) — each step's exit code and output tail, the record that the build ran and the app launched. Derived by `the loop`, absent when the gate never ran. Read it before grading a [ui] row NO EVIDENCE.

t0_artifacts.description: spec-evaluator: per-scope T0 verdict paths for this round. Listed-but-missing/red, or a scoped spec with none → status: failed (structural precondition, not a criterion).

eval_report.description: qa-edge-hunter: the PASS EVAL report — negative-space input; its covered territory is subtracted from charters.

app_url.description: qa-edge-hunter: the running app to hunt (one real request at Q0, not a ping). NULL for a deliverable that is not served over HTTP — a CLI, a library, a batch job — where Q0 drives the binary instead. It was a bare string, so the first genuinely non-UI run could not compile a QA order at all: the payload carries null, the order fails its own schema, and the hunt is skipped for a reason that looks nothing like 'this deliverable has no URL'.

round.description: the round this order is counted against.

HammerCensus.description: The stop census as data — the proposal GATE L4's resolver reads before it lets an answer set say `ship`. Written by the loop's stop step at `.shapeup/<slug>/reports/hammer-census.json` (the name is older than the step), read back against this shape by the loop before GATE H, and stopped on, when it is not this shape. A proposal, never a decision: promotion and shipping stay the PO's call, and the loop never acts on it.

ship_blocking.description: Must-have items that failed the baseline comparison — non-empty exactly when the verdict is cannot-ship.

baseline.description: The baseline the comparison ran against, or null when the pitch's problem statement stood in for it.

RunArgs.description: The launch record — what a run was launched with, resolved once and written to .shapeup/<slug>/run-args.json by `harness init run` in the same act as the receipt. Every switch the operator typed lands here or does nothing: the loop that drives the run reads nothing but this record and the artifacts, and the loop reads `noEval` to refuse writing a PASS report over a run launched with no evaluation. The model floor (sonnet or above for `exec` and, unless `noEval`, `eval`) is enforced when the record is written and again when the loop reads it.
RunArgs.x-location: .shapeup/<slug>/run-args.json — written fresh when a run is opened (and again by `init run --force`); an already-open run keeps the record it has
RunArgs.x-writer: harness init run (kernel), from the same parsed argv as the receipt
RunArgs.x-readers: harness probe next (the loop's state machine), harness reduce ship (the no-evaluation guard), harness probe resume
RunArgs.x-not-here: Run config the LEDGER already carries does NOT get a second home in the record — eval_dimensions, lens, spec_folder, stack, run_cmd, app_url are read off harness-run.md frontmatter, so a copy here would be a second source that can disagree with the first. The record carries what no artifact on disk holds: identity, budgets, the model matrix, pluginRoot, startedAt, and the skip switches (noEval, noQa).

slug.description: The feature slug this run builds — the aggregate root every path is keyed off.

runId.description: The run key, copied from the receipt `harness init run` wrote in the same act. Identity, not run config the ledger already carries; the receipt stays the source of truth.

models.description: The L0.8 role -> model matrix, resolved once: a flag, else SHAPEUP_<ROLE>_MODEL, else sonnet; qa follows exec. The model floor: `exec` and `eval` are sonnet or above, refused at `init run`; `qa` is not checked, and `eval` is not under noEval.

budgets.description: The two record-level circuit breakers (AGENTS.md) — outer round_budget, inner attempt_budget. The third, opt-in DEADLINE breaker (the wall-clock budget) is NOT a record field: it is typed at `harness init run --wall-clock-budget` and lands in the run receipt's `wall_clock_budget_s`, which `harness verify budget` reads directly.

pluginRoot.description: The plugin copy the run was opened against — the root every kernel path in an order is spelled from.

startedAt.description: ISO timestamp the run was opened at, the same instant as the receipt's started_at.

lane.description: The lane the launch asked for (`init run --lane full`). Only the full lane is served; the small-change lane retired and `tiny` is refused at the launch. Never rides in WorkOrderPayload.

noEval.description: If true, skips the EVAL phase completely. Rides here rather than in the ledger because there is no frontmatter line that carries it — contrast eval_dimensions, which does.

noQa.description: If true, skips the QA Edge Hunt (`--no-qa`). Rides here for the same reason as noEval: no frontmatter line carries it. It is declared because the loop reads it — a switch the record omits is a documented flag that does nothing.

maxParallelScopes.description: How many scopes may build at once (`--parallel-scopes`). A dial rather than a constant because concurrency is a COST question before it is a speed one: every extra leg is another worker's full context. 1 restores sequential scope building, which is the mitigation when a worker archetype proves unsafe to run beside itself.

adversarialVerify.description: If true, each FAIL finding gets one independent skeptic before it costs a whole fix round (`--adversarial-verify`). Off by default: it is a pure addition that spends one sub-agent per finding, and the single-judge invariant is unaffected — a refutation retracts a finding, it never issues a verdict.
